---
title: "Concentrations (4.5 and 4.6)"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
source("_prepare.R")
box::use(show = projlib/show, util = projlib/msdial_utils)
tr <- tut$to_report
mat_id <- util$mat_id_of_blank_subtracted(tr[["best normalization"]])
lst <- tut$proc[[mat_id]]
batch <- lst[[1]]
rd <- SumExp::row_df(batch$concn)
# A compound quantified in the samples, with some values below the LLOQ (to show the LOD/LLOQ rules)
ok <- which(rd$has_proper_range %in% TRUE & rd$to_export %in% TRUE)
below <- vapply(ok, function(i) sum(batch$concn[["conc"]][i, ] < rd$lloq[i], na.rm = TRUE), 0)
fid <- rownames(rd)[ok[which.max(below > 0 & below < ncol(batch$concn) / 2)]]
in_log <- isTRUE(tr$params$log_calibration)
```

The last two figures of page 4 show the **result**: the concentrations of the chosen compound
(here **`r rd[fid, "feature_name"]`**, batch `r names(lst)[1]`) in all samples, and its stability
and precision in the QC samples over the whole run.

## 4.5 Concentration per class

```{r}
#| label: figure-4-5
df1 <- SumExp::as_tibble(batch$concn[fid, ])
flag <- if ("conc_flag" %in% names(df1)) df1$conc_flag else NULL
hover <- paste0("<b>", df1$sample_name, "</b><br>", df1$Class, " · batch ", df1$batch_id, " · inj. ",
                df1$injection_order, "<br>conc. ", show$num_txt(df1$conc), " (", show$imputed_kind(df1$conc, df1$lloq), ")")
show$plotly_conc_by_class(conc = df1$conc, lloq = df1$lloq, cats = as.character(df1$Class),
                          cat_colors = tut$class_colors, hover = hover, name = df1$feature_name[1],
                          y_title = paste0("Concentration [", SumExp::metadata(batch$concn)$concentration_unit, "]"),
                          log = in_log, flag = flag)
```

A box per class (QCs, study groups, blanks) with the samples as points. The colour of a point tells
whether its value was **measured** or **replaced** by the LOD/LLOQ rules:

| Point | Signal of the sample | Value |
|---|---|---|
| dark grey: *Measured* | at or above the mean signal of the LLOQ level | the calculated concentration |
| red: *Not detected* | below the LOD signal | LLOQ / 4 |
| orange: *Detected* | from the LOD signal to below the LLOQ level | LLOQ / 2 |
| blue: *Set to LLOQ* | at or above the LLOQ level, but calculated below the LLOQ | the LLOQ |

With the processing option *Replace values below the LOD/LLOQ* unticked, the red and orange values
have no number: they are reported as *n.d.* (not detected) and *n.q.* (not quantified), left out
of the plots and statistics, and their number is given under the title. Use the **Linear / Log**
buttons for the scale.

**How to read it**

- **Differences between the study groups** are what you are after; the QCs should be tight.
- **Many replaced values** in a group mean the compound is mostly below the LLOQ there; its
  average is then driven by the replacement values, so look at the measured values only (the
  exported statistics and report 4.5.1 use measured values only).

## 4.6 QC samples

```{r}
#| label: figure-4-6
# The figure of the app (app/www/quanta_figs.js, copied to assets/ before each render)
show$qc_conc_html("qc-figure", show$conc_figs_data(lst), compound = fid, script_src = "assets/quanta_figs.js")
```

The compound in the QC samples of **all batches** (each batch quantified with its own calibration),
in two views; switch with the buttons above the plot:

- **Control chart**: each QC as its % deviation from the median of its QC group, along the
  injection order. The area is green within the limit of the QC RSD% filter for targeted compounds
  (30% if that filter is not used) and red outside it; the batches are shaded and the purple line
  is the trend (a moving mean within each batch).
- **Per batch**: the QC values of each batch with their mean ± SD and CV% (red above 15%); the
  dashed line is the mean of all batches. **Linear / Log** switch the scale.

The chips next to the buttons count the QCs beyond the limit, and give per QC group the CV% in
each batch and between the batches. Only measured values count for the median, the means and the
CV%; open points are values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules.

**How to read it**

- **Points within the green area** from the start to the end of the run mean the whole procedure
  (normalization, blank subtraction, calibration) gives the same concentration throughout.
- **A step between batches** (the trend jumps, or a high CV% between batches) points to a batch
  effect in the calibration, e.g. a calibration curve of one batch that differs from the others;
  compare the batches' curves in 4.4.
- **A drift within a batch** (the trend slopes) that normalization did not remove points to a
  compound that its internal standard does not follow well (see 3.8).
- **A high CV% within a batch** means the compound is not measured precisely there, even if its
  mean is right.
